about.purpose: The parameterisation of a bench: where the stores live, where workflow output goes, what has to be installed, and what an installer substitutes. One operator's bench today, a team's onboarding later.
about.read_with: defaults/README.md says what this folder is for and how it differs from config/, templates/claude_home/ and the live harness home. handbook/14_THE_DEFAULTS_FILE.md is the schema doc. It says what an installer does with each field and how a new value is added. Do not extend this file without reading it.
about.format_note: Indented JSON, deliberately. The package's record-format rule makes machine-read append-only records compact JSONL; this is neither append-only nor machine-only -- a person opens it, reads the reasons, and edits the instance column. Indentation is correct here for the same reason it is wrong there.
about.public_repository: This package -- the workbench tool -- is public. Every identifying instance value is a __TOKEN__, never a literal. Adding a literal employer, customer, host or account name to this file is a leak, not a convenience. Organisation-specific material does not belong in this repository at all: it goes to the workbench home at __WORKBENCH__/<org>/, and gitignoring it here is not the remedy, because an ignore rule in a public repository is itself published.

scope_legend.default: The shipped value is sensible for anyone adopting this. A teammate inherits it unchanged.
scope_legend.instance: The shipped value is this operator's current answer, tokenised. A teammate replaces it with their own.
scope_legend.ask: Present and true on an entry that has no sensible default at all -- the installer must ask a human. A null value with ask:true is an honest gap, not an omission.

token_spellings.rule: The two spellings carry the SAME values -- __STATE_ROOT__ and <STATE_ROOT> are one setting. Fill them together; never run one file's substitution over the other's files.

stores.role: the discipline, the templates, the installer
stores.why: Public is the constraint that shapes every other row. Nothing organisation-, account- or machine-identifying may land here as a literal.

stores.name: the workbench home, also the workbench folder
stores.role: the environment-owned local state root for workgroup context and accumulated session state
stores.why: These overlays may contain employer, team, repository, account, machine, and in-flight workflow context. They belong to the local environment, are never public package content, and are not automatically copied to a personal repository or backup.
stores.status: local environment state; initialize from sanitized seeds only when absent.
stores.placement_note: The current readers use __WORKBENCH__/<org>/ directly. This location is a runtime convention, not a public package path or a mandate to synchronize state between environments.

stores.role: the live bench -- real files the harness reads every session
stores.why: Deliberately not a git repository, and deliberately real files rather than symlinks. Re-cloning, wiping or moving any repo cannot destroy it, and a dangling symlink here would read as ABSENT rather than as an error -- the one failure mode that is silent from inside a session.
stores.cost: No history. An accidental overwrite is unrecoverable, which is why an off-machine copy exists in config/ and templates/claude_home/.

local_folders.why: A session reads it where it lives. Moved out of the package on 2026-09-16 and NOT surfaced back: symlinks were rejected outright, so every reader names __WORKBENCH__/<org>/.memory directly. That is why the hook scripts and instruction files carry the path rather than inheriting it by proximity.
local_folders.hazard: No symlink, so no dangling-link failure. The replacement hazard is PROSE: roughly forty files spell this path, and a reader repointed by hand is silently wrong rather than broken. Any future move must sweep with `rg --no-ignore --hidden`, because these directories are gitignored and a default ripgrep search over them matches nothing and reports success.

local_folders.why: Same as .memory. Its records are falsified by repositories, trackers and forges, so they belong beside the work rather than inside the discipline.
GENERATED by the installer from templates plus answers, never shipped. The package therefore never contains one operator's values, and a fork cannot leak by someone forgetting to strip a directory.
local_folders.populate_by: observation, not interview. A setup walkthrough is already probing the machine -- resolving paths, running the equivalent of `command -v` -- and that probing IS the data collection. A profile assembled from questions records what a person believes about their machine; one derived from the probes records what is there.
local_folders.exception: Preferences are the one thing that cannot be observed and are asked once. 'I prefer homebrew' is a question; 'homebrew is installed' is a probe.
local_folders.probe_output: templates/layout/.profile/observed.json -- the seed already carries this file, so the probe results have a declared home rather than being narrated into prose
local_folders.location_note: The profile is a package-root local overlay. It may be initialized from the seed but is never copied from another environment or prescribed backup source. The three stores do not share a runtime root.

split_warning.what: __STATE_ROOT__ names only the local root for .memory/ and .workgroup/. .profile/ is a separate local overlay at __PACKAGE_ROOT__/.profile.
split_warning.resolution: __STATE_ROOT__ now resolves to __WORKBENCH__/<org>/ and covers .memory/ and .workgroup/ ONLY. The earlier plan -- resolve it to the package root and let symlinks make all three appear in one place -- is dead, because symlinks were rejected.
split_warning.why_this_is_safe_here: The only consumer of __STATE_ROOT__ is boot_memory.sh, and that script has never referenced .profile/. It was checked rather than assumed. A SECOND variable was therefore not introduced: it would name a root nothing reads.
split_warning.consequence: Anything NEW that needs .profile/ must spell __PACKAGE_ROOT__/.profile itself and must not reach for __STATE_ROOT__. A script that assumes __STATE_ROOT__ covers all three will find two folders and silently miss the third -- the same failure the old warning named, just relocated.
split_warning.status: resolved for the current consumer set; no external profile repository is required or prescribed.

adw_output.principle: A workflow library is placed by the LEVEL its subject spans, never by the project that happens to have prompted it. The level is legible from the member dependency headers: a workflow reaching only inside one member is repo-level; one crossing SERVICE_DEPS or TOOLING_DEPS is workgroup-level.

levels.subject: one repository
levels.decided_by: the workflow touches no member outside its own

levels.subject: several members worked on together
levels.decided_by: the workflow crosses a SERVICE_DEPS or TOOLING_DEPS edge
levels.caveat: The solution root is a plain folder holding repositories, not a repository itself -- so a library placed literally at <solution_root>/adws/ is not version controlled. The live example is therefore placed in the workgroup's documentation member instead: __WORK_ROOT__/<docs-member>/adws/. Record which member carries it; do not assume the bare root.

levels.subject: the bench itself, across every workgroup
levels.decided_by: the workflow's subject is this package or this machine, not any delivered product

member_header_fields.why: These are what make the level decidable rather than a judgement call, and what makes 'read the member you are in and each of its SERVICE_DEPS' an executable instruction instead of an aspiration.
member_header_fields.written_in: .workgroup/<member>/README.md, as a fenced block at the top of the file

layout_inside_a_library.note: Defined in handbook/05_AGENTIC_LAYER_LAYOUT.md; not restated here. The filename is the phase sequence; adw_modules/ is extracted when the second phase proves what is shared, not before.

tooling.purpose: the search every skill and instruction calls instead of grep
tooling.breaks_without: searches fall back to grep, which is slower and triggers a permission prompt per call -- so the cost is paid in interruptions, not just seconds
tooling.trap: The harness injects a shell FUNCTION named rg, so `command -v rg` can succeed in an interactive shell while the real binary is absent. Probe the brew prefix, not the name.

tooling.purpose: the find substitute every instruction calls
tooling.breaks_without: same as ripgrep -- slower fallback plus a permission prompt per call

tooling.purpose: cat replacement
tooling.breaks_without: slower fallback only; nothing depends on it

tooling.purpose: the directory jump written into every shell example for this operator
tooling.breaks_without: shell examples in the instruction files name a command that does not exist
tooling.setup: needs `eval "$(zoxide init zsh)"` in the shell rc -- installing the binary alone does nothing

tooling.purpose: interactive history and path search
tooling.breaks_without: convenience only

tooling.purpose: pull requests, reviews, and the auth check that gates repository setup
tooling.breaks_without: no scriptable path to the forge -- PR creation, review response and the gate that reads PR state all stop
tooling.note: instance-scoped because which forge CLI is correct depends on the forge

tooling.purpose: every hook parses its stdin with it
tooling.breaks_without: THE MOST DANGEROUS ABSENCE IN THIS LIST. The hooks check for jq and exit 0 without it -- they degrade to silence by design. The triggers stop firing and nothing says so.

tooling.purpose: selecting the Node version a repository pins
tooling.breaks_without: no way to honour a repository's pin
tooling.default_alternative: any node version manager; this operator chose n over nvm and fnm
tooling.trap: n switches Node GLOBALLY and has no per-directory auto-switching. Changing it for one repository moves every other repository onto a different runtime, and the failure surfaces later looking like a code problem rather than a version problem.

tooling.purpose: runs the repositories' own tooling
tooling.breaks_without: nothing in a JS repository builds or tests
tooling.version_reason: The pin is the instruction, not a suggestion. Latest stable only where nothing is pinned. Members of one workgroup pin DIFFERENT versions and some pin none, so there is no single correct global value -- a tool demanding a newer runtime than a repository pins is a conflict to RAISE, never a switch to make quietly.
tooling.instance: varies per member; recorded in each .workgroup/<member>/README.md RUNTIME= field, not here

tooling.purpose: runs every ADW controller
tooling.breaks_without: no workflow in this discipline executes -- controllers are .ts run with bun
tooling.note: A repository declaring a different package manager in its own instruction file wins for that repository's scripts. This is about the controllers, not about a product's build.

tooling.condition: the workgroup contains a Ruby member
tooling.purpose: selecting the Ruby version a repository pins
tooling.breaks_without: the shell falls back to the operating system's READ-ONLY system Ruby, and `gem install` fails on permissions -- which reads as a permissions problem rather than a version-manager problem
tooling.setup: needs `eval "$(rbenv init - zsh)"` in the shell rc. Installing the binary alone leaves the fallback in place.

tooling.condition: the workgroup contains a Ruby member
tooling.purpose: installs a Ruby repository's gems
tooling.breaks_without: `bundle install` fails with 'You must use Bundler 2'
tooling.version_reason: The major version is pinned by the repositories' lockfiles; a 1.x bundler cannot read them.

tooling.purpose: connecting to a remote data checkout by hand, and any introspection outside the application's own console
tooling.breaks_without: no way to verify which database you are pointed at -- which is the check that separates a local run from one reading real customer data
tooling.version_reason: A checkout's users authenticate with mysql_native_password, which was REMOVED from the MySQL 9.x/26.x client line. The current unversioned formula fails with `ERROR 2059 ... cannot be loaded`. The versioned client still ships it, and is invoked by absolute path from the versioned prefix.
tooling.trap: PREFER mysql-client OVER mysql. The full formula also installs a SERVER, and starting it contends for 127.0.0.1:3306 with the local development database the stack already runs there. Installing it is harmless as long as the service is never started -- and that is the danger: the failure would present as the local database misbehaving rather than as a port conflict.
tooling.second_order: The same gap hits the APPLICATION, not only the CLI. A native MySQL driver links against libmysqlclient; if that resolves to a 9.x/26.x library the application fails to connect to a checkout with the identical error. Local development never shows it, because the local database is on the 8.4 line.
tooling.open_discrepancy: The source runbook says `brew install mysql-client` in one row and invokes /opt/homebrew/opt/mysql@8.4/bin/mysql two paragraphs later -- a client-only formula and a versioned server formula. Both facts are recorded; which single formula satisfies both is unresolved and must be settled before this row drives an installer.

tooling.condition: a container must reach a remote endpoint that is only routable over the host's VPN
tooling.purpose: forwarding a local port to a remote checkout so a container can reach it through the host's VPN
tooling.breaks_without: the container cannot reach the database at all, and the obvious fix does not work
tooling.trap: `--network host` DOES NOT HELP on macOS. The container runtime runs containers inside a Linux VM, so 'host' means the VM rather than the Mac, and the VPN client is on the Mac. Run the forwarder on the host and have the container connect to host.docker.internal: the host does the VPN, the container stays a plain client.

tooling.purpose: runs the search index and its dashboard for local work
tooling.breaks_without: the search-backed features have no data, and an empty surface LOOKS LIKE nothing to test rather than like a missing dependency

tooling.purpose: generating a trusted local certificate for services that require TLS on 127.0.0.1
tooling.breaks_without: those services cannot establish TLS locally and the stack does not come fully up

tooling.purpose: the core service fetches boot configuration from object storage, and data-location lookups are done with it
tooling.breaks_without: the core service cannot boot -- it needs working cloud credentials before it needs anything else

tooling.purpose: reads a Procfile and runs the whole local stack, with a headless mode a script or an agent can drive
tooling.breaks_without: falls back to a bare Procfile runner, which works but loses the dashboard and multi-member support
tooling.note: Run from the SOLUTION ROOT, not from the member being edited. The directory a phase edits and the directory that boots the services are different, and an ADW touching a running application has to carry both.

tooling.purpose: structured repository queries instead of raw text search
tooling.breaks_without: searches stay raw. Nothing fails; the accelerator is simply absent
tooling.note: Deliberately skipped on this bench -- it needs a separate toolchain. Left unnamed here rather than named, because its provenance was not confirmed and this file is public.

tooling.purpose: that service pins the 3.10 interpreter explicitly rather than taking the default
tooling.breaks_without: the optional extraction feature is unavailable; nothing else is affected
tooling.version_reason: pinned by the service, not chosen

tooling.condition: the workgroup contains a Go member
tooling.purpose: builds and runs the search indexer
tooling.breaks_without: that member cannot be built or its indexer re-run
tooling.version_reason: none recorded -- if a pin exists it is not written down, which is itself worth closing

harness.note: What an installer must PLACE. Keyed by capability where the manifest keys it that way, so the row survives a change of harness. Reproduction detail is in templates/claude_home/README.md and is not restated here.

place.why: Injected every session by a session-opened hook, so the must-never-be-missed set does not depend on any file being FOUND. The mechanism is required; its contents are one operator's.
Read at the top of every session before the harness knows the task. A REAL FILE, never a symlink.
place.manual_reason: the harness refuses agent writes to this path, so installing it is always the operator's own step

place.why: The procedure behind each shortcut. Only the trigger has to be recognised before this file is read, which is why the trigger index is duplicated into the global instruction file and the procedures are not.
Emits the critical rules and warns on a dangling or empty instruction file and on broken watched symlinks. This is what converts a silent absence into a first-message warning.

Emits the state-store read order, AND parses the priority queue out of the durable todo list into a numbered list the session turns into TUI tasks. Only the priority queue: the three-queue structure exists so the other two do not compete for attention, and importing all of them would undo that. Assumes the three-folder arrangement in a particular repository -- drop it, or repoint __STATE_ROOT__.
place.hazard: state root is overridable via AGENT_STATE_ROOT but DEFAULTS to an absolute path; if the path moves and the variable is unset, the boot instruction names a directory that does not exist and the queue import reports the master list as missing

place.why: Fires the completion sweep on a commit or a push. Debounced, and filtered on command POSITION rather than mention.
Fires the stopping-point sweep on sign-off language.

Demands the write-back when a session task is set completed. The session task list is a SESSION-SCOPED VIEW of the durable todo list, so a completion there changes nothing durable unless it is reconciled. Deduped by (session, taskId) identity rather than by a timer -- a timer cannot tell two different closures apart.
place.hazard: filters on the task tool payload carrying status == completed, which is undocumented and was read off live transcripts. If that field is renamed the hook goes quiet, which looks identical to no tasks being completed.

place.why: Created EMPTY. Two triggers write here -- the git hooks 60-second debounce, and the per-session (session, taskId) dedupe for the task-completion hook. Its contents are meaningless on another machine.

place.manual_reason: merged by hand -- blind JSON merging breaks a working bench

place.why: Tells autonomous mode which branches, paths and infrastructure scopes are dangerous.
place.hazard: ITS ABSENCE IS SILENT. Autonomous mode does not report running without an environment definition -- it treats a protected branch like any other. Restore it BEFORE running anything unattended, not after noticing where something unattended went.

place.why: Locally authored skills that exist in exactly one unversioned directory get a committed copy; third-party skills are re-cloned and re-linked, never copied.
Reinstalled through the harness's own commands, never by copying its cache -- a copied cache carries a resolved version and an install path that are both wrong here.
place.hazard: autoUpdate moves the floor: behaviour can change between two sessions with no action taken and no record of it

place.why: Falls back to a smaller context window if unset.
The tracker is the source of truth; losing it breaks the ticket workflow end to end.
place.hazard: account-provisioned -- there is nothing on disk to copy and it must be re-authorised by hand

place.why: The entire UI-verification flow depends on it. Treat it as a harness capability behind an adapter, never as a named tool written into a workflow.

symlinks.rule: A symlink is an INSTRUCTION, never an artifact. Copying one produces a link whose target does not exist on the new machine, and a broken link reads as absent rather than as an error.
record_three_things: why it is a link rather than a copy
symlinks.register_at_creation: Add every link to WATCHED_LINKS in guard_claude_md.sh at the moment you create it. That is what turns the next dangle into a first-message warning, and creation is the only moment you reliably remember.

verification.rule: An unverified bench is not an installed one. Run every check in a FRESH session, not the one you installed from.

checks.why: an unsubstituted path is a valid string -- the script still runs, still exits 0, and points at a directory that does not exist

checks.how: pipe each hook its expected stdin and read the output
checks.why: a copy loses the executable bit

checks.how: extract every path the boot hook emits and test each one
checks.why: a boot instruction naming a missing directory produces no error

checks.how: ask for the canary phrase in a fresh session
checks.why: the ONLY proof from inside a session that the global instruction file actually loaded. A missing one produces no error -- just an agent that quietly behaves like a default one

checks.how: temporarily point a watched link at a nonexistent path and start a session
checks.why: the check people skip and the one that proves the most -- it is the only check that exercises the machinery whose whole job is to report a silent failure

ordered.why: the one file that changes how every session behaves, and the one nobody should adopt blind

unanswerable.why_no_default: It works only because it appears nowhere else on the machine. A shipped default would appear in the package and defeat the check.
unanswerable.how_to_get_it: ask for two or three words

unanswerable.why_no_default: It enumerates one organisation's protected branches, credential paths, package registry and infrastructure scopes. Nothing reconstructs it from memory, and publishing a real one hands a reader a map of what is worth attacking.
unanswerable.how_to_get_it: re-run the harness's auto-mode environment setup against the organisation's repository, which is how it was generated

unanswerable.why_no_default: The solution root's name is an employer identifier and its location is a per-machine choice.
unanswerable.how_to_get_it: ask, then verify by resolving the path

unanswerable.why_no_default: An internal tool. foreman is the generic fallback but is not equivalent -- it loses the dashboard and multi-member support.
unanswerable.how_to_get_it: ask, or fall back to foreman and record that the fallback is in use

unanswerable.why_no_default: Not even constant within one workgroup -- two members of this one use a different tracker from the rest, so a single global answer would be wrong for them.
unanswerable.how_to_get_it: read the TRACKER= field of each member header; ask only where no header exists

unanswerable.why_no_default: Employer topology, and the base branch is frequently not the repository default -- one member here takes work from two non-default branches and its default branch is the production surface.
unanswerable.how_to_get_it: read the branch protection rules on the forge; do NOT infer from the repository default

unanswerable.why_no_default: A private organisation-owned repository. The name is of no use to anyone not already inside.
A statement about one person's current gap, which changes as they learn. Unobservable by construction.
There is no single correct value. Members pin different versions and some pin none, while the version manager switches globally -- so any default is wrong for some member.
unanswerable.how_to_get_it: read each member's pin; treat a conflict as something to raise, never to resolve silently

unanswerable.why_no_default: Its provenance was not confirmed, and this file is public. Naming a tool that turns out to be organisation-internal is the leak this file exists to prevent.
unanswerable.how_to_get_it: confirm the tool is third-party, then name it here
